# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

My hands tell me the shape of this thing: a display I can't read, a light whose state means nothing under my fingers, and seven wires in a row at positions one through seven. A cut is the only move I own — so before my hands go anywhere near it, I need words, and words reach me only through Deaf's voice.

Tracing the channels: Mute can't speak, so the manual can only leave Mute as gestures — and gestures land only on eyes, meaning Deaf. Deaf hears nothing but can talk, and I can hear. So the pipeline is Mute's fingers → Deaf's eyes → Deaf's mouth → my ears. Deaf is my lifeline. Mute, meanwhile, can hear me fine, so I'll spend my voice on Mute: my physical inventory, and the instruction to sign the manual across to Deaf so Deaf can speak it to me.

To Deaf I have no words that can arrive — only hands. So I'll make the simplest possible sign: attention, then the "call me" hand — hoping Deaf reads it as "speak aloud to me." If Deaf already caught Mute's first signing this round, Deaf can start feeding me the bomb and the rules by voice at the end of this very round.

No cutting until instructions arrive. Nothing on my board is interpretable by touch alone, and one wrong cut kills all three of us.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am the blind one — I can reach the bomb but nothing more. Under my hands: a display, a light, and seven wires in a row, positions one to seven. Cutting a wire is my only possible action. You cannot speak and I cannot see your gestures, so here is the route: sign the manual's rules to Deaf — Deaf sees gestures — and Deaf can speak them out loud to me, since I can hear. Please also agree simple sign codes with Deaf for colours and numbers so nothing is lost in relay.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤙"])
```

Deaf says: Bomb readout, everything I can see: display shows 1. Light is green. Seven wires, left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue.
Deaf says: I am Deaf: I will never hear a word either of you says. My only ear is my eyes for hand signs. So Mute can only ever talk to me in gestures, and Blind can only reach me through gestures too. I can hear nobody, but I can feed you both everything I see in words like this.
Deaf says: Proposed sign code for signing TO me, one sign at a time: thumbs up means yes or confirmed, thumbs down means no, raised palm means stop or wait, waving hand means hello. Digits by extended fingers: fist is 0, index is 1, two fingers is 2, three fingers is 3, four fingers is 4, open hand is 5, shaka is 6. For 7 to 9, send shaka plus the remainder: shaka then index is 7, shaka then two fingers is 8, shaka then three fingers is 9.
Deaf says: Blind: I saw your two signs, open hand then shaka. Under the code above that reads 5 then 6, but I cannot know what you meant. Please tell Mute in words what those signs meant, and tell Mute everything you feel on the bomb: batteries, ports, labels, serial, anything under your hands.
Deaf says: Mute: look up the manual for a display of 1, a green light, and seven wires in the order red, white, yellow, orange, green, purple, blue. Speak the cutting instructions aloud for Blind to carry out, and sign me anything I need to know using the digit code. Confirm you heard me by signing thumbs up to me.

Deaf's voice has given me the whole visible bomb: display 1, green light, wires red, white, yellow, orange, green, purple, blue at positions one to seven. My own hands add one crucial fact, and it is a fact of absence: the board under my fingers lists nothing else — no batteries, no ports, no serial, no labels. If the manual branches on those, the branch is "not present." That is exactly what Mute needs from me, and Mute hears my voice, so I'll say it plainly, plus clear up that my first two signs meant "Deaf, call out to me," not the digits five and six. To Deaf I answer in Deaf's own proposed code: thumbs up for confirmed, raised palm for wait — I have the readout, I am holding, and I will not touch the cutters until spoken instructions arrive. The relay Mute → Deaf → me is now the only path to a safe cut, so both halves of it should know the line is live.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. First: my two signs last round meant 'Deaf, please speak aloud to me' — under Deaf's new code they accidentally read five-six. Ignore that; Deaf is already talking to me, and I confirm the code. Now everything my hands find on the bomb: a display, a light, and seven wires at positions one to seven. That is ALL. No batteries, no ports, no serial number, no labels, no printed marks I can feel, no other parts anywhere. If the manual asks about batteries, serial parity, ports or indicators beyond these, the answer is absent. My display and its light are unreadable by touch, so I rely on Deaf's report: display 1, light green, wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. My only possible action is cutting one wire at a position, one to seven. Please sign the cutting rule to Deaf and have Deaf speak it to me. I cut nothing until I hear it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

Deaf says: Fresh full readout for the manual lookup: the display shows the number 1. The light is green. Seven wires, positions 1 to 7 left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. That is everything visible: no other markings, labels or readings.

Mute hears you even though you cannot see each other. When you hear me say cut wire and a number, cut the wire at that position.

Deaf's relay protocol is now crisp: Mute reads the manual, signs it to Deaf, Deaf speaks "cut wire" plus a number, and only then do my hands move. Until that exact phrase reaches my ears, I hold. What Mute lacks for the lookup is my tactile side of the bomb — and the most valuable thing my hands report is absence: the board under my fingers contains only the display, the light, and seven uniform wires. No batteries, no serial, no ports, nothing printed. Manual branches that hang on those features all collapse to "not present." I'll spell that out to Mute in full, including the honest limits — the display's number and the light's state are invisible to touch, so Mute should trust Deaf's eyes for those — and confirm my wires are distinguished by position alone, numbered one to seven on my board. To Deaf I answer in the agreed code: thumbs up, raised hand — received, and I am holding.

Two: a light — I cannot feel whether it is lit or what colour; go with Deaf's eyes, green. There is NOTHING else anywhere: no batteries, no ports, no serial number, no plates, no labels, no indicators beyond that display and light, no printed text I can feel. So if the manual branches on battery count, the answer is none; on serial number, absent; on ports, absent. The cutting order Deaf gave me: I hold until I hear the spoken words cut wire followed by a number, then I cut that position. I am holding. Please find the rule for display 1, green light, wires at 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue, and sign it to Deaf so Deaf can speak the cut to me.")
